note: Benommenheit named as the essential structure of animality; 'the animal can only behave insofar as it is essentially captivated'.
Benehmen/Sichbenehmen = the animal's manner of being, a driven performing (Treiben); set against human comportment (Verhalten) as action.
Behaviour and comportment are 'fundamentally different from one another'; the animal behaves, it does not comport itself toward.
Captivation is 'the inner possibility of behaviour as such', not a state accompanying it.
Bee with severed abdomen carries on sucking — proves no recognition of presence; the bee is 'taken [hingenommen] by its food'.
Driven being-taken excludes recognition of presence and prevents 'taking up a position over and against' the food (Bethe/Rádl sun-orientation experiments).
Captivation = having every apprehending [Vernehmen] of something as something withheld [genommen]; 'no apprehending, but only a behaving [Benehmen]'.

target: the animal does not stand within a manifestness of beings
note: Beings are neither disclosed to nor closed off from the animal; captivation 'stands outside this possibility'.
Behaviour shows an eliminative character (Beseitigen) — devouring or avoidance; the other is there only as prey/partner, in a form of 'away' (weg).
The animal surrounds itself with an Enthemmungsring that prescribes what can occasion its behaviour; 'nothing else can ever penetrate the ring'.
Self-encirclement (Sich-Einringen) open to disinhibition is not encapsulation but the very structure of captivated behaviour; borne along as long as the animal lives.
Heidegger inverts the order: stimulation is possible only where there is prior disinhibition and intrinsic encirclement (against Johannes Müller's Reizbarkeit).
'The organism is the capability for behaviour in the unity of captivation'; 'Captivation is the fundamental essence of the organism'.
Against Buytendijk's 'almost as intimate as the unity of the body itself': the body's unity is grounded in the unity of captivation.
First decisive biological step: sea-urchin embryology establishes wholeness (Ganzheit).
Driesch's neovitalism (appeal to a force/entelechy) repudiated; 'vitalism is just as dangerous as mechanism'.
Second decisive biological step: research on how the animal is bound to its environment (Umwelt).
Uexküll's Umwelt 'means nothing other than what we have characterized as the disinhibiting ring'; the engagement is fruitful but the human world must not be spoken of the same way.
'Captivation is at the same time motility' (Bewegtheit) — an intrinsically determinate motility that unfolds or atrophies; interpretation incomplete without the life-process and death.
Removal of the self-objection: captivation is the condition of the possibility of poverty in world — and of a 'merely comparative' definition from the human standpoint, not the reverse.
Self-objection (§63): 'deprivation' presupposes some knowledge of world; poverty-in-world is conceived only by comparison with man's world-formation, so the thesis 'goes too far'.
The not-having of world was developed under the guidance of the fundamental attunement of profound boredom, 'that as a whole which profound boredom itself manifests to us'.
